problemStatement.formal: For f : Nat -> Real with f nonnegative and antitone on positive indices, prove Summable f iff Summable (fun k => 2^k * f (2^k)).
problemStatement.plain: Generalizes Oresme's grouping argument via the Cauchy condensation test, then recovers divergence of the harmonic series as a special case.
whyMatters: Cauchy condensation turns Oresme's harmonic-series grouping into a general convergence test for monotone nonnegative series.
The proof connects a classical divergence argument with Mathlib's summability infrastructure.
The harmonic-series result is shown both through condensation and in agreement with Mathlib's direct theorem.

proven: The Cauchy condensation test is wrapped for real nonnegative antitone sequences (Lean: cauchy_condensation_test).
The divergence contrapositive is available as cauchy_condensation_diverges.
The file proves the needed nonnegativity and antitone facts for 1/n (Lean: one_div_nonneg_nat and one_div_antitone).
The condensed harmonic series is shown to diverge, yielding Oresme's harmonic divergence proof (Lean: condensed_harmonic_diverges and oresme_via_condensation).
The result is checked against Mathlib's direct harmonic divergence theorem (Lean: harmonic_diverges_mathlib and condensation_iff_summable).
knownResults.goal: Expose the verified Cauchy-condensation characterization and the harmonic-series divergence specialization.

currentState.focus: Completed via PR #8098 (2026-03-30): HarmonicDivergenceOQ04.lean wraps Mathlib's summable_condensed_iff_of_nonneg. 9 theorems, 0 axioms, 0 sorries, 106 lines.

knowledge.progressSummary: COMPLETED: Full formalization of Cauchy condensation test as generalization of Oresme. 9 theorems, 0 axioms, 0 sorries.
insights: Cauchy condensation test completely generalizes Oresme: Summable f <-> Summable (2^k*f(2^k))
Oresme is the special case f(n)=1/n: condensed series = Sigma 1 diverges trivially
Mathlib has full condensation test (summable_condensed_iff_of_nonneg) and Schlomilch generalization
The characterization is biconditional (necessary AND sufficient), not just a sufficient test
